subject: Human Evolution
title: Malaria and Sickle Cell
description: One-minute skill: Malaria and Sickle Cell.

hook.text: Sickle cell disease is devastating. So why hasn't natural selection eliminated the gene?

buildup.text: Malaria kills over 600,000 people a year, mostly in sub-Saharan Africa. It's an ancient killer.

discovery.text: One copy of the sickle cell gene protects against malaria. Two copies cause the disease.

twist.text: In malaria zones, carriers survive better than either non-carriers or sickle cell patients.

climax.text: This 'heterozygote advantage' keeps a harmful gene alive because the trade-off saves more lives overall.

punchline.text: A bad gene survives because half a dose saves lives.

quiz.question: Why does the sickle cell gene persist in some populations?
options: One copy protects against malaria—heterozygote advantage
